newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close sharply down on funds outflow.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close sharply down on funds outflow.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Tuesday as the market's recent sluggishness prompted investors to transfer their funds elsewhere, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 65.05 points or 1.01 percent lower at 6,359.67, near the intra-day bottom of 6,356.05.
Turnover was a modest T$35.96 billion.
The heavily weighted financials suffered strong selling and dropped 1.34 percent, with many investors redirecting funds to the recently hot over-the-counter market, brokers said.
The fledgling over-the-counter market had capped a recent bull run by closing at a five-month high on Monday.

"Investors did not feel confident about buying the high-priced, bigger shares in the main market amid the current slump, so they decided to pull out for now," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.
Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan -- Taiwan's "Big Three" state-run commercial banks -- dropped T$1.50, T$2 and T$1.50 respective to close at T$149.50, T$161 and T$121.
Brokers also noted lack of buying interest from foreign investors.

"Foreign investors usually hold their positions for a longer period than local investors, so the fact that they're not buying now means they are likely to stay out of the market for a few weeks," Chen said.

Scant buying focused on the fundamental-backed electronic shares. Compal Electronics gained T$1 to T$54 and First International Computer rose T$0.30 to T$38.60 as high-tech firms made up six of the session's 10 most heavily traded shares.
Brokers expected a slight rebound for Wednesday, but overall caution is not likely to change. A 6,350-6,420 range was seen.
